summary:
Çankırı province stands under the national framework of Turkey. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct 'contrary to biological sex' with up to 3 years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to 4 years.

Under civil-code article 40, the same draft would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility mandate, with providers facing fines and up to 7 years and patients up to 3 years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected, and Human Rights Watch called for the draft's withdrawal.

The Human Rights Watch article records no province-specific enforcement or incidents in Çankırı.
tangentialFactors: The draft provisions would apply nationwide, including in Çankırı, if enacted; whether the package has since passed is not resolved in the source.
localsOnly: Residents of Çankırı face the same proposed criminal penalties, age floor and infertility mandate on gender-affirming care as the rest of Turkey, subject to the package's enactment status.
outOfScopeNotes: The source is a national-level report on a leaked draft; it provides no Çankırı-specific enforcement, incidents, or local institutional practice. Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted remains unresolved in the inventory.
